transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-14
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~61 minutes
Attendees: leadership + squads (~120)

--- Summary (auto) ---
Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we know it's a packed week so we'll keep it tight. Today: sprint align, decisions on private rollout, and a couple quick ops asks.

--- Topics ---
00:01 Intro and company pulse
06:20 Product priorities and tradeoffs
18:45 Technical deep-dive: routing and canary strategies
33:10 Cost experiments: quantization + batching
44:00 Ops readiness, incidents, and playbooks
55:30 Recap and explicit next steps

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Aisha Kapoor: All right, good morning, um, everyone can you hear me okay? 
[00:03] Crowd / murmurs
[00:05] Aisha Kapoor: Cool. Quick call outline — this is our sprint alignment, gonna be pretty decision focused. Jonas, you want to open with the platform pulse?
[00:14] Jonas Meyer: Yeah, thanks Aisha. So, the last two weeks we saw steady improvements in tail latency, most of the credit to the batching tweaks that SRE pushed. Still seeing a couple of hotspots on long-seq renders, especially for the hybrid KV cache flows.
[00:32] Jonas Meyer: We did run into an incident Tuesday where regional autoscaler didn't pick up burst capacity - that was DC-to-DC failover, we patched it, postmortem is in flight.
[00:45] Emily Chen: (interruption) That incident highlights the need to, um, map out the fallback routing policies, right? We had requests drop because the fallback selected a model variant without the same KV layout, so cache misses spiked.
[01:02] Jonas Meyer: Right. We're proposing to tighten the compatibility matrix for fallbacks — only fallback to variants with compatible KV/layout or fall back to a lower throughput, same-arch option.
[01:18] Priya Singh: On product side I want to be clear: we cannot delay Private customer's rollout for more than three sprints. The legal compliance gating (KMS integration + audit logging) is nearly done, but we need a few more infra items.
[01:35] Aisha Kapoor: Let's put that as a decision point: Do we prioritize Private gating items now, and postpone the noncritical UX polish? We'll vote live.
[01:43] (short pause, lots of tiny voices)
[01:46] Aisha Kapoor: Thumbs up means prioritize Private gating. Thumbs down means keep current roadmap and stretch for both.
[01:52] (visual poll via slack shown on screen)
[02:10] Aisha Kapoor: Looks like overwhelming thumbs up. Okay decision recorded. Priya, your team takes point on the gating checklist.
[02:19] Priya Singh: We'll deliver a canary plan with a gating checklist: KMS/HSM proof, audit log schema, RBAC mappings, and the network smoke tests.
[02:30] Priya Singh: Note: some of the language in the compliance doc got weird in the last pass, the transcription, uh sorry, the template references S L A when it meant SSO in one place — we'll clean that.
[02:42] Jonas Meyer: Technical deep-dive: routing. We have three levers here — region affinity, model variant cost tiering, and latency-first routing. We can't fully optimize all three for every customer, so we propose a default policy for enterprise accounts: region+SLA first, fall back to cost-tier for lower priority jobs.
[03:03] (Q) Marco Alvarez (SRE): How does this interact with Dedicated pools? Like if Dedicated capacity is exhausted, do we route to hosted?
[03:12] Jonas Meyer: Good question. Proposed behavior: try Dedicated pool, then same-region hosted variant, then cross-region hosted variant. If none available, we hit a preconfigured fallback — which could either queue or return a degraded-but-safe response.
[03:25] Emily Chen: Caveat, we need to ensure cross-region fallback respects data residency. Some customers require no cross-border routing. We'll need a flag in the account profile.
[03:35] Priya Singh: That flag must be surfaced in the provisioning UI and infra template. It's a small UX + infra task but critical.
[03:42] Aisha Kapoor: Ok, decision two: add residency flag and require account-level policy. Agreed?
[03:48] (many murmurs, agreed)
[03:50] Aisha Kapoor: Great. Moving to cost experiments — we were asked to choose between an int8 quantization pilot and a more aggressive batching policy as top priority.
[04:00] Liam O'Connor: From infra POV, quantization pilot is safer for correctness — we already have a quant pipeline, the unknown is model quality delta. Batching gains look larger for throughput but they increase tail latency risk.
[04:14] Emily Chen: Also, batching interacts with streaming/real-time use-cases badly. If you push a large batching window, some conversational customers will see lag.
[04:24] Priya Singh: Recommendation: run both in parallel but on separate model subsets — quantization on stable, smaller models with eval sets; aggressive batching on internal low-latency tolerant workloads for measurement only.
[04:37] Aisha Kapoor: Who owns the measurement plan?
[04:39] Priya Singh: Product to own metrics, Liam and Emily to own bench infra. We'll define metrics: p50/p90/p99, cost_per_token, semantic-drift score from eval prompts.
[04:49] Jonas Meyer: Add to that a regression alert: if sem-drift > threshold or p99 increases > 15% we abort.
[04:56] Marco Alvarez: (SRE) We'll automate the abort hook in the pipeline.
[05:00] Aisha Kapoor: Good. Moving on — quick Ops readiness check. Marco?
[05:05] Marco Alvarez: We're soliciting two teams to volunteer for the dedicated pilot next week. Need runbooks updated for new routing fallback and KV cache rehydration steps. We did a dry run internally on Tuesday, found gaps in the cache warming section.
[05:17] Emily Chen: I'll add those to the SRE playbook stub.
[05:20] Nora Patel: Data question — will we keep telemetry for Private customers? Retention windows differ per contract.
[05:25] Priya Singh: Yes, telemetry will be export-only and respect retention policy. We will not hold raw customer prompts in the central telemetry for Private; we'll keep hashes and derived metrics. Legal signoff pending.
[05:36] Aisha Kapoor: Quick nuts-and-bolts: sprint will start Monday. We'll freeze non-blocking feature merges Thursday to ensure time for rollout testing.
[05:44] (someone off-mic) Speaker 8: Does freeze include small docs/website updates?
[05:47] Aisha Kapoor: Docs updates that impact onboarding can be merged; everything else waits.
[05:52] Jonas Meyer: Incident note — we need better tracing for KV cache misses. Emily, can your team add a trace flag we can toggle?
[05:58] Emily Chen: Yes, we can, but it will require a small perf hit when enabled. We'll make it opt-in.
[06:04] (audible keyboard sounds)
[06:10] Audience question / chat: Are there plans to expand Dedicated regions in APAC?
[06:14] Aisha Kapoor: Short answer: yes, next quarter planning includes APAC Dedicated feasibility, but not in this sprint. We'll share more in the region planning doc.
[06:22] Priya Singh: Also, quick ask to sales/growth folks listening — we need two willing customers to run the canary on Dedicated next week. If you have prospects that can commit, send to Aisha.
[06:31] Aisha Kapoor: All right, let's move to rapid-fire updates from leads. Liam?
[06:35] Liam O'Connor: Infra's primary focus is the quant benchmarks and making the autoscaler more proactive. ETA for autoscaler improvements: mid-sprint.
[06:43] Marco Alvarez: SRE will run the regional failover drill next Tuesday 2pm PT. Please make sure on-call is staffed.
[06:50] Nora Patel: Data infra — we'll supply the eval prompts and the metric harness by Friday.
[06:55] Priya Singh: Product will produce the gating checklist by Thursday end of day.
[06:58] (crosstalk, light laughter)
[07:03] Audience member (Sales): Quick question about pricing: if we do private deployments, how will pricing differ?
[07:09] Aisha Kapoor: We'll follow the Dedicated pricing model with a private deployment premium for on-prem installs. Pricing will be contractual and discussed with finance on a case-by-case. AE folks, coordinate with pricing ops.
[07:20] Jonas Meyer: Technical reminder — private deployments need KMS integration, audit log pipeline, and a hardened image. That's the gating checklist.
[07:30] Aisha Kapoor: OK—last 10 minutes: open floor for blockers.
[07:32] Speaker 12 (Eng): We're blocked on a vendor kernel that regresses seq2seq performance in long runs. Is there a rolling mitigation?
[07:40] Emily Chen: We're rolling a fallback kernel and testing it now. If it passes, we'll ship as hotfix.
[07:48] Speaker 15 (Legal): On audit logs — need to confirm retention and encryption in transit and at rest — which KMS are we referencing?
[07:56] Priya Singh: We'll use the standard cloud K M S integration for hosted, and for Private we will support customer-managed HSMs. We'll put the options in the checklist.
[08:07] (pause)
[08:10] Aisha Kapoor: All right team, quick recap and explicit next steps — Priya, run the gating checklist, Liam run quant bench, Emily SRE playbook, Marco schedule the failover drill. We'll reconvene next Friday for a short status sync.
[08:27] Aisha Kapoor: Any final comments?
[08:30] (few voices; 'thanks', 'great')
[08:33] Aisha Kapoor: Cool — meeting adjourned. Thanks everyone.

--- End of transcript ---
